claims.quote: Our successors of the not distant future will surely succeed.
claims.description: Humans will soon succeed in building a working flying machine (stated as the popular view the author goes on to doubt).

claims.quote: The demonstration that no possible combination of known substances, known forms of machinery, and known forms of force can be united in a practicable machine by which men shall fly long distances through the air, seems to the writer as complete as it is possible for the demonstration of any physical fact to be.
claims.description: Heavier-than-air powered flight over long distances is impossible with known materials, machinery and forms of force.

claims.quote: The only satisfaction we can feel in our treatment of the great geometrical problems of antiquity is that we have shown their solution to be impossible. The mathematician of to-day admits that he can neither square the circle, duplicate the cube or trisect the angle. May not our mechanicians, in like manner, be ultimately forced to admit that aerial flight is one of that great class of problems with which man can never cope
claims.description: Aerial flight may be an inherently unsolvable problem like squaring the circle.

claims.quote: Still, considering mere possibilities, it is not impossible that the twentieth century may be destined to make known natural forces which will enable us to fly from continent to continent with a speed far exceeding that of the bird.
claims.description: New natural forces discovered in the twentieth century may enable intercontinental flight faster than birds.

claims.quote: then may men build, not merely airships, but ships which shall fly above the air, and transport their passengers from continent to continent with the speed of the celestial motions.
claims.description: If gravitation can be understood and controlled, ships could fly above the atmosphere carrying passengers between continents at celestial speeds.

claims.quote: We are peering into the law of gravitation itself with the full hope of discovering something in its origin which may enable us to evade its action.
claims.description: Scientists may discover the origin of gravity and a way to evade or control its action.

claims.quote: let us discover some way of reversing the law of gravitation so that matter may be repelled by the earth instead of attracted—then we may have a flying-machine.
claims.description: A hypothetical gravity-repelling technology would make flying machines possible.

claims.quote: It may certainly seem singular if man is never to discover any combination of substances which, under the influence of some such agency as an electric current, shall expand and contract like a muscle.
claims.description: Artificial muscle-like materials that contract under electric current might eventually be discovered, though not soon.

claims.quote: he might find the result to be, ideally at least, a ship which would be driven through the air by a steam-engine with a velocity far exceeding that of the fleetest Atlantic liner.
claims.description: A huge rigid steel-framed dirigible airship over 200 feet in diameter and ~1000 feet long, steam-driven, could outpace the fastest Atlantic liner.

claims.quote: Even if a dirigible balloon should cross the Atlantic, it does not follow that it could compete with the steamship in carrying passengers and freight.
claims.description: Airships would likely not be commercially competitive with steamships for passengers and freight.

claims.quote: Yes, a sufficient number of humming-birds, if we could combine their forces, would carry an aerial excursion party of human beings through the air.
claims.description: Combining many small flying machines or birds could carry a human passenger.

claims.quote: Why more attempts have not been made to apply this system, with two sets of sails whirling in opposite directions, I do not know. Were there any possibility of making a flying-machine, it would seem that we should look in this direction.
claims.description: A flying machine with counter-rotating horizontal rotors (helicopter-like) is the most promising design direction.

claims.quote: Such a project is as futile as can well be imagined; no known substance would begin to resist the necessary pressure.
claims.description: A vacuum balloon (evacuated thin shell) cannot be built because no material could withstand the pressure.
